items.followUp: What appears on the webpage and in the browser tab for this code: <html><body><title>My Page</title></body></html>?

rubric.why: The title element's contents are not displayed in the webpage area.
rubric.description: States that the webpage area is blank.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that no text is displayed in the webpage area or that the page is blank.

rubric.why: The text inside the title element is used as the document title.
rubric.description: Identifies the document or browser-tab title.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving BISERAWALPINDI as the title.

modelAnswer: No text is displayed in the webpage area; the page is blank.
BISERAWALPINDI appears as the document title in the browser tab.

items.followUp: Explain how an IP address helps a computer communicate over a network.

rubric.why: An IP address is a numerical address assigned to a device on a network.
rubric.description: Defines an IP address as a numerical address assigned to a device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an IP address as a numerical address or stating that it is assigned to a device.

rubric.why: An IP address identifies a device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an IP address identifies a device on a network.

rubric.why: IP addresses help network devices direct data to its destination.
rubric.description: Describes the role of IP addresses in directing data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning data routing or directing data to its destination.

rubric.why: An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is commonly written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
rubric.description: Gives a correct IPv4 format detail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that IPv4 is 32 bits or written as four decimal numbers.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a numerical address assigned to a device on a network.
It identifies the device on the network.
Network devices use IP addresses to route data to the correct destination.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is commonly written as four decimal numbers separated by dots, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: What is validation of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Verification is the process of checking whether an algorithm or solution is correct.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying verification checks or tests correctness.

rubric.why: Verification checks that the algorithm produces expected results and meets its requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning expected results or requirements.

modelAnswer: Verification is the process of checking an algorithm or solution for correctness.
It confirms that the algorithm produces expected results and meets its requirements.
